title: The Bigfoot expedition field guide
seo: How to plan a Bigfoot expedition: gear, trail cams, tracks and safety
desc: A practical Bigfoot research guide: where to look, gear checklist, trail cameras, audio and wood knocks, night protocol, casting tracks, common misidentifications, safety and ethics.
lede: Where to go, what to pack, how to set cameras and recorders, what to do when the woods go quiet, and how to bring home evidence that's worth something. Everything we'd tell a friend before their first trip.
blurb: The full playbook: picking a spot, gear, cameras, audio, night sits, tracks, hair, safety and ethics.

title: UFO and UAP skywatching: a field guide
seo: UFO skywatching guide: tools to rule out Starlink, planes and planets
desc: How to skywatch for UFOs and UAP: dark-sky spots, flight and satellite trackers, camera settings, what to write down, the most common lookalikes and where to report.
lede: Most lights in the sky have boring answers, and that's the point: once you can rule out the satellites, planes, planets and lanterns in a few minutes, the ones left over get a lot more interesting.
blurb: Dark-sky spots, the apps that rule out Starlink and planes, camera settings, and the usual suspects.

title: Dogman and night encounters: staying safe and reading the dark
seo: Night encounters guide: eyeshine colour chart, night sounds and safety
desc: What to do if something is watching you in the dark: staying safe, an eyeshine colour and height chart for North American animals, night sounds that fool people, and how to document it.
lede: Two eyes in the headlamp beam at the wrong height. A growl from the treeline. Here's how to stay safe in the moment, work out what was probably looking back, and record it properly.
blurb: An eyeshine colour and height chart, the night sounds that fool everyone, and what to do in the moment.

title: Trail cameras for cryptid research
seo: Trail camera setup guide: placement, height, settings and the rules
desc: How to choose, place and set a trail camera for wildlife and cryptid research: height and angle, settings, batteries, theft protection, baiting rules and checking the regulations.
lede: A trail camera is the one researcher who never gets bored, cold or sleepy. Set it up well and it'll show you everything that walks past. Set it up badly and it'll show you 4,000 photos of a waving fern.
blurb: Choosing a camera, height and angle, settings, theft-proofing, bait ethics and the rules on public land.

title: How to photograph, measure and cast a track
seo: How to cast a footprint with dental stone or plaster (step by step)
desc: Step-by-step guide to documenting a track: photographing with scale, measuring length, width and stride, and casting with dental stone or plaster in mud, dust and snow.
lede: A good track is evidence for about as long as it takes the next rain to arrive. Photos come first, measurements second, the cast last. Here's how to do all three so the result is worth keeping.
blurb: Photos with scale, the measurements that matter, and dental stone casting step by step.

title: How to write a credible encounter report
seo: How to report a Bigfoot, UFO or cryptid sighting credibly
desc: What makes an encounter report credible, how to photograph and keep evidence, protecting your privacy and other people's, and where to send Bigfoot, UFO and cryptid reports.
lede: The best reports aren't the most dramatic ones. They're the ones written fast, kept honest, and full of the boring details that let someone else check them.
blurb: What makes a report hold up, keeping original files, privacy, and where to send it.
